newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke unsure if Germany to hit EMU deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: Welteke unsure if Germany to hit EMU deficit goal.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday it was not yet clear to him whether Germany would be able to reduce its deficit levels enough to qualify on time for European monetary union.
"I do not yet see quite clearly if Germany will be able to fulfill the three percent (deficit) goal," Welteke told a conference in the northern German town of Kiel.
Participants in the first wave of EMU in 1999 have to push their deficit levels down towards three percent of gross domestic product by the end of this year.

Welteke said German finance minister Theo Waigel's stated intention to cut the deficit to 2.9 percent in 1997 was based on the assumption that Germany would be able to achieve strong growth in employment this year.

"From what I have heard about the unemployment data due on Thursday, the trend is not going in the right direction," Welteke said. A weekend newspaper report said unemployment, already at a post-war record, would rise yet further for February.
But he added: "Neither the three percent (deficit) nor the 60 percent (national debt-to GDP) criteria are criteria that must lead to a country not joining (EMU) if it breaches them.
Welteke added that the Maastricht Treaty allowed scope in interpreting a country's adherence to the debt and deficit criteria.
